text: Recent visitor feedback for the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library highlights ongoing issues with the timed-entry ticketing system, which requires advance online purchase and leaves no option for walk-up tickets. Several reviews mention frustration with parking, describing narrow lanes and limited camper spaces, as well as poor signage and communication about security and ticket availability upon arrival. Crowding and long lines at security checkpoints were also noted as problems. While many visitors appreciated the interactive exhibits and architecture, the challenges with access and visitor flow have negatively affected the overall experience for some. Addressing these operational concerns could improve visitor satisfaction.

windows.7: Recent visitor feedback highlights issues with ticketing and parking that need attention. Several reviewers noted confusion about the requirement to purchase tickets online in advance, with no option to buy them at the library, leading to wasted trips. Parking was also criticized, especially for larger vehicles like campers, with concerns about narrow traffic circles and limited camper parking spaces. Additionally, some visitors experienced long lines and poor communication about security procedures and ticket availability while waiting outside, with no restrooms available during this time. On the positive side, interactive exhibits and the architecture received favorable mentions, but these operational challenges are affecting the overall visitor experience.

windows.60: Visitors have frequently noted issues with the timed entry system, particularly the requirement to purchase tickets online well in advance, which has led to frustration and some being turned away after traveling long distances. Parking and traffic flow around the library have also been criticized for narrow lanes, limited camper parking, and poor signage. Several reviews mention long lines and inadequate communication about security and ticket availability at the parking lot.
